title: They left the book: three questions
outcomes: Asks what a surprising move changed and what it threatens before choosing a move
Checks which of his own pieces are loose
Decides whether an offered pawn is a gift or bait by looking at what the capture opens

steps.text: When an opponent leaves the book (plays a move outside the usual opening lines), ask three things before you move. **What did their move change?** A square, a line, a piece. **What does it threaten?** Is any of my pieces loose (attacked and not defended)? **Which habit helps?** The centre, development, castling. Answer the first two before the third.

steps.caption: After 1.e4 g5. The g-pawn attacks nothing. Which habit applies?

line.say: Black's bishop looks along the long diagonal toward d4.

steps.text: An odd move may offer a pawn. Before you take it, run the questions on the position **after** your capture: what does the capture open, and what will it let the opponent attack? Sometimes the pawn is a gift. Sometimes it is bait.

steps.title: Gift or bait?
steps.prompt: An opponent offers a pawn with ...f5. Predict whether taking it is right, then check.
Think of the last time an opponent played something you did not recognise. Which of the three questions did you skip: what it changed, what it threatened, or which habit helps?
